item1.justification: The trace correctly invokes element-by-element anticipation analysis for §102 claims and applies Graham/KSR factors (scope and content, differences, PHOSITA level, secondary considerations, motivation to combine) for all §103 rejections, using the appropriate statutory frameworks throughout.

item2.justification: All rejections cite specific prior art references (US-2013321456-A1 and US-2016247051-A1) and map specific claim elements (e.g., hybrid map data, vector/raster rendering engines, complexity threshold, mobile optimization) to corresponding disclosures in those references.

item3.justification: Stage consistency is maintained: claims found not novel at §102 are carried forward as §102 rejections in the office action and final decision, claims found novel but obvious at §103 are rejected under §103, and claims 21-22 found novel and non-obvious at both stages are allowed—no contradictions between stages.

item4.justification: The examiner has moderate strictness (0.547) and high claim breadth (0.864), which is reflected in aggressively reading prior art broadly to anticipate or render obvious most claims (1-20) while allowing only the narrowly specific HTML/HTML5 claims (21-22), consistent with a broad-interpreter profile at moderate strictness.

item5.justification: The final decision to reject claims 1-20 and allow claims 21-22 follows directly from the accumulated §102 and §103 analyses, with the summary explicitly tying the rejection grounds to the specific prior art findings established in prior stages.
